edges.description: Inflammatory and metabolic injury drives fibrotic remodeling and an arrhythmia substrate.
Fibrotic injury drives maladaptive ventricular remodeling.
The fibrotic substrate underlies re-entrant ventricular arrhythmias.
Inflammatory and fibrotic damage to the atrioventricular conduction axis produces block that can progress to complete heart block requiring pacing.
The same fibrotic damage falls characteristically on the right bundle and the left anterior fascicle, giving the bifascicular pattern that is the hallmark early electrocardiographic finding.
The remodeling cascade manifests clinically as Chagas cardiomyopathy.
The dilated, poorly contracting ventricle decompensates into congestive heart failure, which is now a leading indication for transplantation in South America.
A dilated, aperistaltic colon fails to propel stool, which is the refractory constipation that brings these patients to attention.

Insecticide-based control of domestic triatomine populations removes the vectorial route by which metacyclic trypomastigotes reach a human host, so the initiating intracellular infection never occurs.

nodes.description: Antiparasitic therapy with benznidazole or nifurtimox, the only two WHO-recognized trypanocidal drugs. Efficacy is highest in the acute phase, congenital infection, and early chronic (indeterminate) infection; in established chronic cardiomyopathy the BENEFIT trial showed it clears parasitemia but does not halt cardiac deterioration.

nodes.description: Right bundle branch block (complete or incomplete), characteristically combined with left anterior fascicular block (the bifascicular pattern), is the hallmark early ECG finding of Chagas heart disease and a diagnostic clue in at-risk populations. Bound to the generic Bundle branch block term because HPO lacks a non-complete "right bundle branch block" term (only complete HP:0011712 and incomplete HP:6000313).

nodes.description: Low-grade parasite persistence in the myocardium sustains a chronic interferon-gamma/TNF-alpha-rich Th1 myocarditis over decades. Persistence is supported by the BENEFIT trial, in which the majority of patients with established chronic cardiomyopathy were PCR-positive for the parasite at baseline; about 30% of infected patients eventually develop chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy.

nodes.description: Inflammatory invasion of the enteric plexuses causes progressive destruction of myenteric (Auerbach) neurons throughout the digestive tract. The resulting intrinsic denervation impairs peristalsis and, in a subset of patients, produces the digestive megasyndromes (megaesophagus and megacolon).
